title: Stop the catalogue read surfaces repeating a free claim whose evidence is expired or uncheckable
objective: PR #79 closed the staleness path on /catalogue/categories. PR #83 (S5) closed it on the three adviser endpoints and introduced app/read_api/currency.py. The catalogue READ surfaces were untouched and still served frozen values: offer.zero_cost_class (a stored column), confidence_label derived from material_facts.confidence (frozen at publish), and freshness read from material_facts.confidence_signals or a provider column (also frozen). No clock reached any of them, so they did not merely omit a currency signal -- they AFFIRMATIVELY ASSERTED maximum freshness on evidence that had decayed. This slice threads a read-time clock into every catalogue surface that repeats a class, a confidence label or a freshness figure, caps what those surfaces may assert, and adds evidence currency as a filter dimension distinct from the zero-cost classification.
measured_premise: P1 MEASURED: base re-derived with `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` = f033017d9a76db53491cb35c2ad15512fd7e6a20, equal to the SHA the brief stated. Confirmed rather than trusted.

P2 MEASURED baseline on an ISOLATED PostgreSQL 16 (own container `slice2-postgres`, port 55434, own volume `slice2_pgdata` -- never the shared freetier-atlas-postgres-1 on 5432): `pytest tests/unit tests/integration tests/security -q` -> 2839 passed, 3 skipped, exit 0. tests/security was INCLUDED, unlike the S5 baseline which omitted it and paid for it.

P3 MEASURED the surface inventory at RUNTIME from GET /openapi.json, resolving every 200-response schema through $ref and collecting reachable property names -- deliberately not from the diff, because a route the diff does not touch is exactly the one that gets missed. ELEVEN routes carry a class / confidence / freshness figure: 2 adviser (closed by S5) and NINE catalogue. The brief named only five. The four it missed are /catalogue/compare (the full field set, and it is the side-by-side 'which of these is free' view), /catalogue/offers/{id}/evidence, /catalogue/offers/{id}/history and /catalogue/providers. Instrument floor: an impossible sentinel field name scored 0 hits across all 27 routes and 16 routes matched nothing, so the matcher could both miss and discriminate.

P4 MEASURED that two agreeing sources were both wrong about the size of the router: the brief says '11-endpoint read router' and router.py's own docstring says 'Seven GET endpoints'. Runtime says TEN catalogue routes, nine of which carry a figure.

P5 MEASURED a blind spot in my own instrument before banking its negative: all 10 admin routes reported zero fields, but they are annotated `dict[str, Any]`, so the schema walk cannot see inside them. Re-measured structurally instead: `zero_cost_class|confidence|freshness|completeness` has ZERO occurrences anywhere in apps/api/app/admin/*.py. The negative holds, by a second instrument, under a stated condition.

P6 MEASURED and REFUTED a cost the brief priced into the search-filter decision: `offer.zero_cost_class` has NO index. Migration 0003 creates the column with a CHECK constraint only; the model declares `mapped_column(Text, nullable=False)` with no index=True; no sa.Index names it anywhere. There is no index to lose.

P7 MEASURED and REFUTED the second stated cost: fetch_evidence_currency issues EXACTLY ONE SELECT joining Evidence -> Snapshot -> Source and folds in Python. It is O(1) queries, not N+1. Its real cost was being UNSCOPED (it loaded every evidence row in the database to serve one offer), which this slice fixes with an optional offer_version_ids filter that never changes a verdict.

P8 MEASURED and REFUTED MY OWN scoping hypothesis. I proposed splitting the two provider-aggregate routes into a separate slice on the theory that provider.freshness_score is a stored column needing its own design decision. It is declared in models/domain.py:78-79, read in read_api/service.py:163-164, and WRITTEN NOWHERE in application code, with zero occurrences across all of tests/. Confirmed at runtime on a real seven-provider corpus: 0 of 7 providers have a non-NULL score column. The fallback branch is therefore the only real path, and it averages the SAME frozen per-offer signal the offer surfaces serve. Splitting would have shipped an interval where ProviderHeader rendered 'Data freshness 90%' directly above OfferCards reading 'Freshness Unknown', from the same underlying number. Hypothesis withdrawn; one slice.

P9 MEASURED the real corpus through the real ingest+publish pipeline over committed fixtures for all seven shipped providers (cloudflare is F005; aws, azure, gcp, github, oracle, vercel are the six merged F008 providers): 7 providers, 6 published offers (5 Z0_TRUE_FREE, 1 Z2_TEMPORARY_OR_CONDITIONAL), 38 evidence rows linked to a published version, 0 with a NULL fetched_at. This independently reproduces the S5 contract's P7 figure.

P10 MEASURED the defect itself on that corpus: _provider_scores() returned freshness=1.0 for cloudflare and github via the fallback branch, while the SAME rows read at now+5y yield 0 current and 6 stale. The frozen figure does not move; the world does.

P11 MEASURED the real refresh window, which is not the one the tests use: EVERY source in the shipped provider configs declares schedule='official_pages'. That token is in neither the named vocabulary (hourly/daily/weekly/monthly) nor the compact <n><unit> form, so parse_schedule_window falls back to DEFAULT_STALENESS_WINDOW for the ENTIRE real catalogue. The real window is 7 days. Instrument floor: 'weekly' parses to exactly 7 days and an impossible token falls back, so the parser was genuinely exercised.

P12 MEASURED that the web already handles the None-versus-0.0 distinction correctly, so the requirement reduces to a hard API rule: formatSignal(null) -> 'Unknown' and formatSignal(0) -> '0%'. The API must emit null, never 0.0, for an unchecked claim. Asserted directly as a test.

P13 MEASURED that a staleness vocabulary ALREADY SHIPS in apps/web/src/catalogue/vocab.ts (COVERAGE_MEANINGS.stale: label 'Stale', hourglass icon, 'past its refresh window and needs re-checking'), used only by the category matrix from PR #79. This slice reuses it rather than inventing a second visual language for the same concept.

P14 MEASURED the npm lockfile claim independently and found a SECOND lockfile the brief does not mention. Before: apps/web/package-lock.json = 98f786c2bb0d2e9152d66e6b7ba7b5c3b54b580e, root package-lock.json = 737f99159e586d54de5671ec2aab35117a99025d. `npm ci` installed 336 packages; after: both blobs IDENTICAL, `git status` reports neither as modified, and the lockfiles still carry 423 public registry URLs. npm install and npm audit fix were NOT run. Consequence: Playwright could not be installed into apps/web without rewriting package.json and the lockfile, so browser tooling was installed SESSION-SCOPED outside the repository.

P15 MEASURED, and it refuted a mechanism I had planned: snapshot.fetched_at is NOT NULL. Three independent sources agree -- the ORM annotates it Mapped[datetime] (not optional), information_schema reports is_nullable='NO', and a raw UPDATE to NULL is rejected by the constraint while a NEGATIVE CONTROL update with a real value is accepted. Therefore assess_currency's `fetched_at is None -> UNCHECKED` branch is TEST-COVERED BUT NOT REACHABLE FROM REAL INPUT via the snapshot path. On real data UNCHECKED arises only when the anchor is absent from the index entirely.

coverage_claims_stated_precisely.freshness_reachability: AC-R: `EvidenceCurrency.freshness()` had FOUR call sites at base, all in tests/unit/test_evidence_currency.py, none in application code -- a TEST-COVERAGE fact. REAL-INPUT REACHABILITY was measured separately on the real corpus: 6 of 6 offer-version anchors yield a freshness() value. This slice gives it its first production consumers (OfferDetail.freshness, CompareOffer.freshness, provider freshness, and EvidenceCurrencyOut.freshness).
coverage_claims_stated_precisely.provider_score_columns: AC-P: measured structurally (never written in app code, 0 occurrences in tests) AND confirmed at runtime (0 of 7 providers non-NULL on a real ingested corpus). Both statements are made; they are different questions.
coverage_claims_stated_precisely.unchecked_branch: assess_currency(None, ...) is TEST-COVERED but NOT REAL-INPUT REACHABLE through the snapshot path, because of the NOT NULL constraint measured in P15.

search_filter_decision.question: The S5 contract recorded this as a known deferred problem: /catalogue/search filters on the STORED offer.zero_cost_class column in SQL, so the moment display changes, filter and display disagree.
search_filter_decision.options_measured: A (filter on recomputed currency): the two costs the brief priced -- 'no SQL index' and 'possible N+1' -- were both MEASURED AND REFUTED (P6, P7). A-prime (id-first two-phase) makes it cheap: N integers rather than N object graphs. B (post-filter the page): DISQUALIFIED BY ARITHMETIC, not taste -- PAGE_SIZE is 20 and total_results/total_pages are computed from the PRE-filter count, so a page renders fewer rows than it claims, a page can render zero rows while later pages still have results, and total_pages is wrong. It replaces a false freshness claim with a false count.
search_filter_decision.decision: Option C. zero_cost_class keeps its SQL filter and its exact meaning ('classified Z0_TRUE_FREE'); evidence currency becomes a SEPARATE, opt-in `evidence_current` dimension implemented by the A-prime two-phase mechanism so total_results stays honest whenever it is used.
search_filter_decision.why_not_cost: Cost could not decide it once both priced costs were refuted. Three measured reasons decided it: (1) both SHIPPED precedents display rather than omit -- S5 routes a stale Z0 to a `stale` partition and still shows it because 'suppressing a free offer is its own defect', and PR #79 renders a stale pair as coverage state `stale` rather than removing it from the matrix; filtering search would make it the ONLY surface in the product that hides them. (2) A wrongly-omitted free offer is a defect of equal severity, and an omission is INVISIBLE to the reader in a way a label is not. (3) zero_cost_class classifies the offer's TERMS and currency is a property of the EVIDENCE; conflating them in one filter was arguably the original error.
search_filter_decision.residual_risk_accepted: A client that reads only zero_cost_class and ignores evidence_currency still renders a stale claim as free. Mitigated by shipping the API and the web changes in the SAME slice and by the browser evidence, not by the API alone.

response_shape.additive: New EvidenceCurrencyOut block (current, checked, stale, freshness, age_days, window_days, oldest_fetched_at, reason) attached to ProviderSummary/ProviderDetail, OfferSummary, OfferDetail, OfferState, OfferVersionOut, SearchResultItem, CompareOffer and OfferEvidenceResponse. Purely additive, so existing consumers keep working.
response_shape.value_changes: confidence_label capped by the EXISTING confidence_label_for() the adviser already uses (one definition, two surfaces). OfferDetail.freshness and CompareOffer.freshness become live currency.freshness(). Provider freshness becomes a None-aware mean over LIVE per-offer values. advanced.score and advanced.signals are WITHHELD when the evidence is not current -- the recommendation offered at plan time, taken because no override was returned -- because the publish-time signal dict contains a `freshness` key that read 1.0 on five-year-expired evidence and is therefore an unsupported assertion, not merely a stale one. The reason is not lost: it is carried in plain language by evidence_currency.reason.
response_shape.new_filter: GET /catalogue/search?evidence_current=true|false. Omitted means 'any', which is the default, so nothing is hidden unless asked.

acceptance_criteria: AC1 Each of the NINE catalogue surfaces stops repeating an unsupported free claim when the backing evidence is expired.

AC2 PAIRED CONTROL on each of the nine: the same surface still serves a supported free claim when the evidence is current. A guard that cannot be shown to PERMIT is indistinguishable from one that broke the product.

AC3 The zero-cost classification is never HIDDEN, on any surface. A stale Z0 offer is returned and labelled, because a wrongly-omitted free offer is a defect of equal severity to a wrongly-published one.
AC4 confidence_label collapses to 'unknown' for a non-current claim and is untouched for a current one.
AC5 advanced.score and advanced.signals are withheld for a non-current claim and intact for a current one.
AC6 freshness is recomputed at read time, never served from the frozen publish-time signal.

AC7 freshness is None -- never 0.0 -- when no check was possible, and 0.0 remains a legitimate MEASUREMENT for a checked claim at or past its boundary. The two are distinguishable on the wire and on the page.
AC8 evidence_current is a filter dimension separate from zero_cost_class, and total_results/total_pages remain honest when it is used.
AC9 A serializer given NO currency context fails closed to 'cannot assert currency', never to 'current'.
AC10 fetch_stale_offer_version_ids semantics are unchanged, proved by TRANSCRIBING the old derivation rather than importing it.

AC11 EVERY new guard is proved able to FAIL by mutation: baseline GREEN, anchor matched EXACTLY ONCE, patched line printed READ BACK FROM DISK, RED observed with the failing test NAMED, restored and proved byte-exact by BOTH git hash-object AND a raw byte comparison.
AC12 BROWSER evidence: a real browser against the running stack shows what a user sees for an expired claim, a current claim, and the currency filter.
AC13 Full suite green with the collected test count strictly increasing and none lost.
AC14 feature_list.json byte-identical to base; progress.md append-only proved by RAW BYTE PREFIX with a NEGATIVE CONTROL.

expiry_mechanism.chosen: Mechanism G (NEW): the one-second boundary differential.
expiry_mechanism.how_it_works: assess_staleness decides stale = age > window, a STRICT inequality. Every per-surface test reads the SAME unmodified rows at two clocks one second apart, straddling that boundary: at fetched_at + window the age equals the window and the claim is current; at fetched_at + window + 1s it is stale. No timestamp is backdated, no schedule is shrunk, no ingest is re-run -- only the clock advances, by the smallest increment the comparison can resolve.
expiry_mechanism.why_it_is_the_strongest_available: All six spent mechanisms move DATA or a SCHEDULE, so a surface could in principle respond for the wrong reason. G moves only the clock, through the seam production uses. A surface serving a FROZEN value CANNOT flip on a one-second change -- which gives the instrument its impossible-value floor: identical output either side of the boundary would be a positive detection of the defect being fixed. Asserted directly by test_the_boundary_is_a_real_discontinuity_one_second_wide before anything is built on it.
expiry_mechanism.mechanism_h_refuted: A second new mechanism was planned -- Snapshot.fetched_at = NULL with the Evidence row still present, reaching UNCHECKED through a different code path than a missing anchor. It is IMPOSSIBLE: the column is NOT NULL (P15). Recorded as a refutation with its negative control, and the reachable route to UNCHECKED (detaching the evidence from the version) is exercised instead.
expiry_mechanism.reused_and_declared: Backdating Snapshot.fetched_at (spent mechanism 1) is REUSED for the browser-evidence seed only, and is declared as such. The browser needs persisted data at the real wall clock; the load-bearing proof is mechanism G in the suite.

errors_made: E1 Opened by running `git reset --hard <sha>` to 'reset to main' WITHOUT first checking HEAD, which was already at f033017d. The command was unnecessary and destructive-shaped. Plan mode blocked it; my care did not. Care is not a mechanism.

E2 Trusted two agreeing sources about the router's size -- the brief's '11-endpoint read router' and router.py's own 'Seven GET endpoints'. Runtime says ten. Two sources agreeing is not corroboration when neither was measured.

E3 Printed 'all 10 admin routes carry none' as a clean negative before noticing that `dict[str, Any]` made the schema walk blind there. Caught one step late, and only because a field count of exactly 0 looked wrong.

E4 Diagnosed a hung probe as 'CPU-bound on the seven-provider HTML ingest' from two consistent symptoms (high CPU, no database activity) and ASSERTED it twice. The real cause was an infinite loop in my own path-discovery code: the probe walked up from __file__ looking for alembic.ini, but it lives OUTSIDE the repo, so it spun forever at the drive root where the parent of a drive root is itself. I inferred a cause from symptoms without testing the cause.
E5 A bulk regex rewrite of print( -> say( also rewrote print(message) INSIDE the say() function, creating infinite recursion. Caught before it ran, but only by reading the diff.

E6 Wrote the first mutation-control harness to pass multiple pytest paths as ONE space-joined string, so pytest looked for a single file with a space in its name and exited 4. The harness correctly refused to proceed (baseline not green) rather than reporting a false result -- but four controls were silently skipped on that run, and a second run with a multi-line anchor silently matched zero times because of line-ending mismatch. Both are now handled explicitly.

E7 Committed the browser-evidence corpus -- including a snapshot backdated by 1824 days -- into the SAME database the test suite uses, and the next full run reported 48 failures that were pure contamination, not a code defect. 'Use your own database' was not sufficient; the seed needed its own too. Resolved by dropping and recreating the schema, after which the suite returned 2862 passed.

E8 Wrote a provider-rollup test that read at the expiry boundary. The rollup spans every published offer, whose snapshots are stamped microseconds apart during one ingest, so a sibling offer was already one microsecond past its own window and the test failed intermittently. It was caught by the mutation harness's baseline-green gate rather than by me.

data_security_privacy_portability_z0.data: No migration, no schema change, no Alembic revision, no stored projection, no fixture capture edited. Currency is recomputed on every read against a caller-supplied clock (decision Q11: a stored projection becomes a second source of truth that silently goes stale, which is the precise failure being fixed).
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.security_privacy: No secret introduced. No registry URL, internal hostname or credential written to any repository file, commit message, PR body or report. npm ci was run and BOTH lockfiles verified blob-identical afterwards; npm install and npm audit fix were NOT run. Playwright was installed SESSION-SCOPED outside the repository precisely because installing it into apps/web would have rewritten package.json and the lockfile. A local .impeccable/ tool cache containing absolute machine paths was deleted rather than committed.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.portability: No new runtime dependency, no new mandatory service. The web change adds one component and reuses the existing badge tones and staleness vocabulary.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.z0: This is the Z0 honesty path. The failure being closed is a free claim repeated on nine public read surfaces after the evidence supporting it expired -- and, on two of them, an affirmative assertion of MAXIMUM freshness. The gate fails closed on both shapes of non-currency, while the paired controls keep a genuinely free, freshly-evidenced offer fully served and fully promoted: a wrongly-withdrawn free offer is a defect of equal severity.

l2_disposition.result: FAILED on one narrow blocking defect; everything else independently verified clean.
l2_disposition.blocker: apps/web/src/catalogue/OfferCard.tsx gated the '$0 with no billing risk' promise on `detail.evidence_currency?.current !== false`. With the field ABSENT, `undefined !== false` is TRUE, so the unconditional promise rendered while the badge two lines above simultaneously read 'Truly free -- not verified'. The evaluator reproduced it in a real browser with the field stripped in flight: the promise rendered THREE TIMES, with both paired controls firing.
l2_disposition.why_my_reachability_call_was_wrong: I checked reachability at a SINGLE VERSION -- field always emitted, TS field required on all eight response types, one render site fed only from API responses, no caching. All true, and all irrelevant. The population I failed to widen to is API/SPA VERSION SKEW: verified independently on base main, apps/api/app/read_api/schemas.py has ZERO occurrences of evidence_currency (the 15 repo-side hits are the adviser path and a query helper) and apps/web has zero, while docker-compose.yml builds api and web as SEPARATE images. A newer web bundle against an older api image receives no field at all. A required TypeScript field constrains what we COMPILE against, never what an older server SENDS.
l2_disposition.fix: One expression. Both gates now ask `currencyMeaning(...).underminesClaim` -- the SAME function the badge already used -- so the rule exists once instead of twice in two disagreeing forms. Deliberately NOT a second independent condition, because the defect was that the rule was stated twice.
l2_disposition.tests_added: Four, in apps/web/src/catalogue/components.test.tsx. OfferCard had NO render test at all before, which is why the defect survived: absent -> no promise (the blocker), stale -> no promise, present+current -> promise DOES render (paired control, so a fixed gate is distinguishable from one that hides everything), plus a gate-agreement test asserting badge and description never disagree across all three currency states.
l2_disposition.mutation_control: Restoring the old fail-open expression turns exactly ONE test red -- the ABSENT-case blocker -- and no others, so the new test attributes precisely. OfferCard.tsx restored byte-exactly afterwards (blob 869d07b9, 5660 bytes, hash AND raw bytes).
